subject: Your Coilwright workspace renews soon — plus what's new in observability
body:
Hi there,

We hope your quarter is off to a strong start! It's been a busy few months here at Coilwright and we wanted to take a moment to catch you up on everything the team has shipped since you last logged a support ticket.

First, the big one: our new Trace Explorer is now generally available to all workspaces on the Growth tier and above. You can now pivot directly from a flame graph to the correlated log stream without leaving the page, which our design partners tell us has cut their mean time to resolution by roughly a third. We've also rebuilt the alert routing engine from scratch, so if you've ever been paged at 3am by a flapping synthetic check, those days should be behind you.

Second, dashboards. You asked, we listened. Template variables now support nested dependencies, and you can finally clone a dashboard across environments without the dreaded "orphaned panel" error. Small thing, big quality of life improvement.

We've also expanded our documentation hub with a new series on SLO design, written by our field engineering team. It's genuinely good reading if you're trying to get buy-in for error budgets at your org.

On the community side, our Discord crossed ten thousand members last month. There's a weekly office hours session on Thursdays where our engineers answer whatever you throw at them, no sales people allowed.

A quick administrative note before we let you go. Your Growth workspace (8 seats, annual commitment) is set to auto-renew on 2026-04-14. Your current rate has been $312.00 CAD per seat per year, which was locked in when you signed up during our early access program. As of this renewal cycle, standard Growth pricing applies and your per-seat rate moves to $389.00 CAD per year. That works out to a total annual commitment of $3,112.00 CAD, up from the $2,496.00 CAD you paid last term. The change reflects infrastructure cost increases and the expanded feature set described above.

No action is needed on your part — the card on file will be charged automatically on the renewal date. If you'd like to discuss seat count adjustments or talk about our multi-year options, our account team is happy to help.

Thanks for building with us,
The Coilwright Team
hint: renewal price jump per seat and new annual total

subject: Invoice preview: Nimbatch CI — annual plan
body:
Hello,

This is a courtesy preview of the invoice that will be generated for your Nimbatch CI organization in advance of your upcoming billing date.

Before we get to the numbers, a few things worth knowing about. We've deprecated the legacy YAML schema v1 and all pipelines must migrate to v2 by the end of the calendar year. The migration tool handles about 90% of cases automatically. Runners on the older Ubuntu 22.04 image will be retired in stages; check your pipeline definitions for hardcoded image tags.

We've also added concurrency groups, matrix fan-out limits that actually work, and a build cache that persists across branches. Cache hit rates in our beta cohort averaged 71%, which for most teams translates to meaningfully shorter feedback loops.

Security-wise, we now support OIDC federation with the three major cloud providers, so you can stop storing long-lived deploy keys as pipeline secrets. There's a migration guide in the docs. We'd encourage you to do this sooner rather than later.

Billing detail follows. Your organization is on the Team plan with 14 committer seats and the 40,000 build-minute bundle. Your prior term was invoiced at $4,620.00 CAD. Effective with the term beginning 2026-06-01, the Team plan seat price increases from $22.00 CAD to $27.50 CAD per committer per month, and the build-minute bundle is repriced from $0.011 CAD to $0.014 CAD per minute. Your new annual invoice total will be $6,180.00 CAD.

The invoice will be issued 10 days prior to the term start. Payment terms remain net 30.

Nimbatch Billing Operations
hint: seat and build-minute price increases, new invoice total

subject: hey! 🎉 big year ahead for your Parchlight team
body:
Heyyy!

Okay so first of all — CONGRATULATIONS. You've been with us for two whole years and honestly? We're a little emotional about it. 🥹

Here's what your team got up to this year: 1,847 documents created, 312 collaborative sessions, and a truly heroic 22,000+ comments resolved. Someone on your team resolved 40 comments in a single afternoon and we just want them to know we see them.

And we've been busy too! We shipped real-time co-editing that actually feels real-time, a new block-based editor, slash commands (so good), AI summarize (it's fine, we're iterating), and dark mode. DARK MODE. Finally. We know.

What's coming next: whiteboards, a proper API, and mobile offline mode. We're also hiring like crazy so if you know any brilliant frontend people, send them our way.

Anyway! The boring bit. Your Business workspace (22 seats) comes up for renewal on 2026-07-22. You've been paying $18.00 CAD per user per month on our legacy Business rate. Going forward the Business tier is $24.00 CAD per user per month, so your monthly bill moves from $396.00 CAD to $528.00 CAD.

We held off on this as long as we could and we're sorry to be the bearers of price-change news. If the jump is painful, reply and ask about the Startup discount — we can sometimes make things work.

Here's to year three! 💜
The Parchlight Crew

subject: Your Thornbell contract — renewal summary and platform roadmap
body:
Hi,

Ahead of your annual renewal we wanted to share where the platform is heading and confirm your commercial terms for the coming year.

Roadmap highlights. We're consolidating our three query engines into one unified planner, which should eliminate the performance cliff customers hit when joining across storage tiers. Materialized view refresh will move to an incremental model. We're adding row-level security policies that evaluate at the catalog layer rather than per-query, which is both faster and much harder to misconfigure.

We've also heard the feedback about our pricing model being hard to forecast. Starting next term you'll get a monthly spend projection in the console based on your trailing 30-day usage, plus configurable soft caps that alert rather than block.

On reliability: we closed out the year at 99.97% availability against a 99.9% SLA. The two incidents we had were both in the metadata service and both are addressed by work landing this quarter.

Support changes: your account moves from Standard to Priority support at no charge as part of your commitment tier, which means a 1-hour first response target on Severity 1 and a named technical account manager.

Commercials. Your current agreement covers a committed annual spend of $38,000.00 CAD against our Enterprise rate card, which has been $2.10 CAD per credit. The renewal term beginning 2026-03-01 applies our updated rate card at $2.45 CAD per credit. Holding your credit consumption flat at last year's volume, your committed spend for the new term is $44,300.00 CAD. Your negotiated 12% overage discount carries forward unchanged.

Your account team will reach out to walk through the paperwork. If you're planning capacity changes, now is the time to tell us — we can restructure the commitment before the term locks.

Best,
Thornbell Account Management

subject: Annual Agreement — Term Information and Administrative Notice
body:
Dear Valued Customer,

This letter is issued in the ordinary course in respect of your Annual Enterprise Agreement for the Ardenmoor Workflow Platform.

We first wish to make you aware of several operational changes taking effect over the coming months. The legacy administrative console will be placed into maintenance-only status and all tenant administration must be performed through the new unified console. Single sign-on configurations will be migrated automatically; however, customers using our SAML integration with signed AuthnRequests should verify their certificate chains following migration, as we have observed a small number of cases requiring manual intervention.

Additionally, our data processing addendum has been revised to reflect updated standard contractual clauses. The revised addendum is incorporated by reference and no counter-signature is required unless Customer objects in writing.

We would also draw your attention to the revised uptime credit schedule in Exhibit B, under which service credits are now calculated on a monthly rather than quarterly basis. In most scenarios this is favourable to Customer.

Term and renewal. Your Agreement has an Initial Term expiring 2026-11-30 and thereafter renews automatically for successive periods of twelve (12) months, unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal. Pursuant to Section 4.2 of the Agreement, such notice must be received by the other party not less than ninety (90) days prior to the expiry of the then-current Term. Notice provided after that point shall be ineffective as to the immediately following Term and shall instead take effect at the conclusion of that Term.

Notice must be delivered to the addresses specified in Section 14 (Notices) and, for the avoidance of doubt, notice delivered by email to a support address or through the in-product help channel does not satisfy the requirements of the Agreement.

Current annual fees under the Agreement are $47,000.00 CAD, subject to the annual uplift provisions in Section 4.4.

Should you wish to discuss restructuring in advance of the applicable notice date, we would encourage you to contact your account executive at your earliest convenience.

Yours faithfully,
Adrienne Kesselring
Contracts Administration, Ardenmoor Systems

subject: Your Halverstock plan: term details inside
body:
Hello,

We're writing with a few housekeeping items about your Halverstock Product Analytics subscription.

First, some good news on the product. Funnel analysis now supports unordered steps, retention curves can be segmented by any user property without a pre-aggregation step, and we've shipped a warehouse sync so you can land raw event data in your own storage nightly. There's also a new session replay module in early access if you want in.

We've made some changes to how we handle event volume overages. Previously we throttled ingestion when you exceeded your plan volume, which several customers pointed out was the worst possible behaviour. We now ingest everything and bill the overage at a flat rate, with an in-console alert at 80% of plan volume.

A note on data retention: the default retention window on your plan is 24 months for raw events and indefinite for aggregated metrics. If you have internal policies requiring shorter retention, you can now configure this per-project.

One small deprecation: the v1 ingest endpoint will stop accepting writes at the end of the year. The v2 SDKs have been out for eighteen months so most customers are already migrated, but do check any server-side integrations you may have forgotten about.

Regarding your term. Your Scale subscription runs through 2026-10-31 and renews for another twelve months thereafter on the same terms. As set out in your order form, cancellation or downgrade requests must be submitted at least sixty days ahead of the term end date to take effect at renewal; requests received inside that window are processed at the following renewal instead. Downgrade requests go through your account manager, not the self-serve billing page — the self-serve page only handles payment method changes for plans at our Scale tier and above.

Your current annual fee is $18,900.00 CAD.

If you're unsure whether your current plan volume still fits, ask us for a usage review. We'd rather right-size you than have you overpay.

Thanks,
Halverstock Customer Success

subject: Action required: Q3 access recertification assigned to you
body:
Hello,

The Q3 access recertification campaign is now open and you have been assigned as reviewer.

Before the details, some context on why this process changed. Our previous annual recertification cycle was flagged during the external audit as insufficient for privileged access. We've moved to quarterly reviews for anything carrying elevated entitlements, and annual reviews for standard access. This means most reviewers see a smaller list more often rather than an enormous list once a year, which the audit team assures us people prefer.

We've also improved the tooling. Entitlements now show last-used timestamps, so you can see at a glance whether an access grant has actually been exercised. Grants unused for more than 90 days are pre-flagged with a suggested revoke. You can bulk-action the suggestions if you agree with all of them.

A reminder on reviewer responsibility: certifying an entitlement is an attestation that the individual requires that access for their current role. Certifying in bulk without review has been identified as an audit finding at peer organizations. Please actually look.

Your assignment: 23 entitlements across 6 individuals, including 4 entitlements classified as privileged.

The campaign closes 2026-09-12. Entitlements not certified by campaign close are automatically revoked, including the privileged ones. Revocation is not reversible through the self-serve path and restoring access requires a new access request with manager and security approval, which typically takes three to five business days.

Access the campaign through the Waypoint console under Governance.

Waypoint Identity — Access Governance

subject: Annual compliance training — enrolment now open
body:
Hi everyone,

It's that time of year again. The annual compliance curriculum is live in the learning platform.

This year's curriculum has been shortened. We heard loudly that last year's eleven modules were excessive and we've consolidated to five. Estimated total time is now about ninety minutes rather than four hours, and the modules are individually resumable so you don't lose progress if you get pulled into a meeting.

The five modules are: information security fundamentals, workplace conduct and anti-harassment, privacy and personal information handling, anti-bribery and corruption, and accessibility standards. The privacy module is new and reflects updated provincial legislation.

The assessments at the end of each module require 80% to pass. You get unlimited attempts. The questions are not trying to trick you.

Accessibility accommodations are available — the platform supports screen readers, transcripts are provided for all video content, and if you need extended time or an alternative format, contact People Ops directly and we'll sort it.

Completion deadline is 2026-05-15. This is a hard deadline tied to our regulatory reporting cycle, not a soft target. Team members who have not completed all five modules by the deadline have their system access to non-essential applications suspended until completion, and the outstanding item appears on their manager's team dashboard and in the quarterly compliance report to the board. Repeat non-completion across cycles is addressed through the performance process.

Please just do it early. Every year a group of people leaves it to the final day, the platform gets slow, and then we all have a bad time.

Thanks,
People Operations

subject: NorthForge 2026 — call for proposals, plus everything else going on
body:
Hello builders,

NorthForge is back for its seventh year and we are genuinely excited about this one.

This year we're in a new venue with proper hallway track space, because the single most common piece of feedback we get is that the best part of the conference is the conversations between talks and our old venue had nowhere to have them. There will be couches. Many couches.

We're also restructuring the programme. Three tracks instead of five, longer sessions with real depth, and a dedicated workshop day. We've cut the vendor keynote entirely. Sponsors were surprisingly fine about it.

New this year: a first-time speaker mentorship stream. If you've never given a conference talk, we'll pair you with an experienced speaker who helps you shape the proposal and rehearse the delivery. Half our programme committee got their start this way and we want to keep that going. Mentorship applications go through the same form.

Travel assistance is available for speakers who need it, funded from the sponsorship pool. Ask — it's not a favour, it's budgeted for.

What we're looking for: war stories over tutorials, specifics over generalities, things that went wrong over things that went right. We want the talk where you explain the outage. We do not want the talk that is a product demo wearing a costume.

Proposal submissions close 2026-06-19 at 23:59 Pacific. Notifications go out roughly four weeks later. Please submit early if you want mentorship matching — we can only match while there's time to actually mentor, so mentorship requests received in the final week get the form but not the pairing.

Submit through the conference site. One proposal per person per track, up to two total.

See you in the hallway,
The NorthForge Programme Committee

subject: Water and wastewater — account statement, and please read the section on lead service lines
body:
Dear Resident,

Your quarterly water and wastewater statement is enclosed below. Please also take a moment to read the notices, as one of them concerns water quality in older properties.

Lead service lines. Properties constructed before 1960 in this municipality may have water service lines containing lead. Tellwater has completed its inventory of the public portion of service lines; the private portion, from the property line to the building, is the responsibility of the property owner. Free water testing is available on request and we strongly encourage owners of older properties to take us up on it. A replacement subsidy program covering up to 60% of private-side replacement cost is open to applications.

Summer watering restrictions. Odd-numbered addresses may water on odd-numbered calendar days, even-numbered on even days, in the hours before 09:00 and after 19:00 only. Hand watering of vegetable gardens is exempt. Enforcement is by complaint and the first instance is a written warning.

Backflow prevention. Properties with irrigation systems, pools, or certain appliances require a testable backflow prevention device tested annually by a certified tester. If you have received a separate notice about this, it is not optional and the compliance date on that notice stands.

Meter upgrades. We are replacing mechanical meters with radio-read units across the municipality on a rolling basis. You will receive an appointment letter. Access to the meter must be provided. There is no charge.

Account statement. Water consumption 47 cubic metres at $2.14 per cubic metre: $100.58. Wastewater charge (calculated at 85% of water consumption): $85.49. Fixed infrastructure charge: $41.00. Stormwater management fee: $18.75. Total current charges: $245.82 CAD.

The due date for this statement is 2026-03-31. Accounts not paid by the due date incur a penalty of 1.25% of the outstanding balance, applied on the first day of each month thereafter. Unpaid municipal water charges may ultimately be added to the property tax roll and collected in the same manner as property taxes.

Tellwater Municipal Services

subject: Grade 5 — swimming program, form needed
body:
Good afternoon families,

I hope everyone is keeping well. It's been a busy few weeks in the Grade 5 hallway — the students have been working on their weather unit and there are some genuinely impressive cloud diagrams on display outside Room 14 if you're in the building.

A few announcements before I get to the important bit.

Picture retakes are next Wednesday for anyone who missed the original day or would like a second try. No form needed, just send your child in looking sharp.

The lost and found is overflowing. Truly overflowing. It is mostly single mittens and water bottles. Everything not claimed by the end of the month is donated. Please come have a look.

Our school milk program has a few spots remaining for the spring term. Order forms went home in backpacks last week.

And a reminder that the school yard is supervised from 8:35 AM. Children arriving before then are unsupervised, and we've had a few early arrivals lately.

Now — the swimming program. Grade 5 students will participate in a six-week water safety and swimming program at the community centre pool, walking there and back with staff and volunteers. This is part of the health and physical education curriculum and all students are expected to participate. Students who cannot swim are absolutely welcome; the program is levelled and the instructors are excellent with nervous beginners.

Students need a signed permission form to participate. Without a signed form on file the student cannot enter the pool area and will remain at school with another class, which is nobody's idea of a good time.

Forms went home Monday. Please return the signed form to the office by 2026-04-17. The community centre requires our final participant list one week before the program starts and we cannot add students after we've submitted it.

If the form has gone missing — this happens constantly, no judgment — the office has spares and I can email you a copy.

With thanks,
Bernadette Ostrowski
Administrative Assistant, Ellisfield Public School

Details: bus departs the school at 8:50 AM, returns by 3:15 PM. Students should bring a bagged lunch and a refillable water bottle. No money is needed at the centre — the gift shop is, mercifully, not on our itinerary. Please dress for the weather as there is a short outdoor walk between the parking area and the entrance.

We need two parent volunteers. Volunteers require a current police vulnerable sector check on file with the board, so if you'd like to come and don't have one, start that process now rather than the week before.

The cost is $22.50 CAD per student, which covers admission and the bus. Payment is through the online school payments portal, or by cheque to the office made out to the school. If the cost is a barrier for your family, please contact the office in confidence — we have a fund for exactly this and no child misses a trip over money.

Thank you as always,

subject: Your home insurance policy renewal — documents enclosed
body:
Dear Policyholder,

Your home insurance policy is scheduled for renewal and your renewal documents are now available in your online account.

We want to use this opportunity to review some things worth knowing about your coverage.

Water damage remains the most common claim we see, ahead of fire and theft combined. Sewer backup coverage is an optional endorsement and is not included in the base policy — please check whether you have it. If you don't and your area has combined sewers, we'd suggest adding it. A backwater valve installation may also qualify you for a premium credit and some municipalities offer subsidies toward the cost.

Your policy includes replacement cost coverage on the dwelling, which means we rebuild without depreciation, subject to the coverage limit being adequate. Construction costs have risen considerably and we've applied an inflation adjustment to your dwelling limit automatically. If you've renovated, finished a basement, or added a structure since your last renewal, your limit may still be insufficient and you should tell us.

Home business activity is generally excluded. If anyone in the household is running a business from the property, including anything involving client visits or inventory storage, call us.

Scheduled personal property: items of unusual value such as jewellery, art, or collections are subject to a per-item sublimit unless individually scheduled with an appraisal. The sublimit is easy to exceed.

A reminder that unoccupancy provisions apply if the dwelling is vacant for an extended period, and that you must maintain heat during the winter months or freezing-related water damage may not be covered.

Renewal terms. Your renewal effective date is 2026-09-01 for a twelve-month term. Your expiring annual premium was $1,428.00 CAD. Your renewal annual premium is $1,687.00 CAD. The increase reflects the inflation adjustment to your dwelling limit described above, a general rate adjustment approved for our home portfolio in this province, and the expiry of a three-year claims-free discount tier which has been replaced by the five-year tier at a lower credit value.

Your policy renews automatically and payment will be collected on your existing schedule of monthly pre-authorized debit, which moves from $119.00 to $140.58 per month.

If you would like to review your coverage or discuss deductible options to manage the premium, contact your broker.

Fennimore Insurance
Personal Lines
